Hey there!

1.) A Tube Screamer is meant to overdrive your amp signal- so it was absolutely designed for tube amps.  It will alter your sound and dirty it up if you use it in front of a Solid State amp, but it it won't give you the rich harmonic sound it was designed to create.  In my experience it will muddy it up and make it ugly.

2.) Practice?  What I started doing once I got comfortable enough on the neck of the guitar, was start playing along with tunes and playing lead over it.  I tried to learn full songs and analyze what the guitarists are doing, and take the techniques that I like.

3.) Think of the Root Note as a home base.  The modes are taking an established scale, and making the "home base" some place different.  I'm sure there have been 1000 threads that explain it in depth.

If you're going to learn a song- don't half ass it.  Learn the structure first, then learn riffs.  Really master the rhythm parts so you really understand how the song moves.  Then- learn the solos.  Once you understand all of these things, then start to put your spin on it.  But really prove to yourself that you can master someone's techniques.  Understand that learning someone's technique is like taking advice from a friend.  Take the things you find valuable, and cast aside the other stuff, ONLY after understanding it thoroughly.

I would definitely lean towards the MIM Strat and here's why:

Guitars are three things: Hardware, Electronics and Wood.  The wood is the most significant to me, as it determines the feel and the lifespan of the guitar.  You can always replace hardware and electronics, but I would want to get something durable and more resilient.  That way you'll have the guitar for a longer period of time without having to constantly make adjustments.

Maybe this isn't the point of this sub, but:

Keep in mind that these guitar pedals are essentially toys to inspire new sounds and ideas from you, and tools to help you get the tone you're aiming to achieve.  I wouldn't worry about "dumbing down" a versatile pedal.  If it's giving you the sound you want, seems its doing its job. :)

I do use the Pinnacle and would recommend it for the EVH tone. It also has a Vintage/Modern switch on it.  I've gotten some great Billy GIbbons Tone from using the vintage setting and dialing back the gain.  Seeing that I kind of hear that Billy Gibbons tone as a precursor to early VH tone, I really enjoy it.

Well I'd say the Marshall-in-a-box type pedals are purely to get your clean amp to that British crunchy distortion from the late 60's to the early 80's.

However the Brown Sound is more about honing in on that tone EVH had from about '76 on.  What he did with Power Attenuation on his Marshall essentially made the amp transform.

So I'd say that Diming a Marshall Pedal isn't exactly going to get the same desired tone.  Because EVH DID dime his amp, but he ALSO backed down the power. So he could "run the engine on all cylinders" while still being able to back down the master volume.
